title: Answer squash-chain review 2 and build the chain landing rule
summary: Read as two parts in one change: revise the squash-chain design with a response appendix answering review 2's six findings, then build the revised design (athena.candidate/2, core writes the fields, chain-aware landing rule in the gate, jobs::check and history changes, tests, doc updates). R2-M1 is answered by a stated assumption about how previous_job is derived.

defaults_applied.how: The design is revised to answer review 2 before the build, and D69 is settled.
New landing, jobs and history tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
All code in Rust; only markdown docs otherwise.
Behavior criteria are cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Hidden requirements (the review's fixes, the design's follow-up list, doc pointers) were recovered from the repository.
The response appendix cites the code lines it checked and labels untested claims.
The chain rule is enforced by the gate with tests, not prose.

assumptions: 'Answer review 2' means revise the design doc with a response appendix (as was done for review 1), then implement the revised design as D69 describes it.
The three review-1 decisions stay at the author's assumed defaults (recorded order, refuse rules-file changes, refuse multi-parent chains), since the user never changed them.

For R2-M1, previous_job is derived by the core as the job whose landing is the latest landed job in the base commit's history; absent when none exists. A job based on an unlanded predecessor candidate is out of scope for chain linking.
Governance files (athena.toml, workflows, etc.) are not changed; no records/ changes.
This is one large change covering docs, schema, core, and gate; the follow-up list of design §5 is built in full.
question: Review 2 (R2-M1) found nothing says where previous_job comes from. I assumed the core derives it as the latest landed job in the base commit's history (absent if none). Should the user name it instead?

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md gains an Appendix B answering every review-2 finding (R2-M1, R2-m1, R2-m2, R2-m3, R2-n1, R2-n2) with a disposition and the section changed; the review file itself is unchanged.
The design defines how the core derives previous_job from the base commit (including after a hand change or records-only commit) and states the stated assumption.

The design fixes R2-m2 (one remaining job, how a landed predecessor is found at P, /1 predecessor) and R2-m1 (merge-commit message), and corrects the schema work to name AnyRecord, the schema-name table and its consumers in athena-core run.rs/store.rs and athena-gate jobs.rs.
athena.candidate/2 with base_fingerprint and previous_job exists in athena-data; /1 still loads; athena-core writes both fields when it builds a candidate.

D69 in docs/decisions.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/records.md, docs/enforcement.md and the v0 design section 7.3 are updated to say the chain rule is built; D69 is settled as accepted or changed with a reason.

Run `cargo test`: all pass, including new landing_tests.rs cases: hand-built two-job chain lands first; each §4.3 refusal; repeating and no-op fingerprints; rules-file change; two-parent refusal; partly landed chain; per-check refusals on a middle job; missing middle job; jobs::check and history repeat-job tests.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.
Run `cargo test` to confirm a single-job landing and a /1 candidate behave exactly as before (existing landing tests unchanged and passing).

out_of_scope: Signing records or defending against forged records
Chains whose predecessor has not landed on the base branch
Changes to athena.toml, workflows or other governance files
departures: The reference forecast is from typical small changes. This request is a design revision plus a multi-crate build of the gate's most sensitive rule with many tests, so cost, time and risk are much higher, and the user is more likely to intervene.
